name: security-subscription-entitlement-lifecycle-review
intent: Subscription state changes and actual product capability grants
artifacts: Provider events, plan mapping, trial/grace/cancel state and enforcement at protected product operations.
trace: Trace plan identity and payment state into server capability checks, including downgrade/cancellation and delayed webhook replay.
experiment: In an owned billing fixture compare an active entitled action with the same action after an effective downgrade or canceled synthetic subscription.
disproof: A retained badge or documented grace period is not a privilege bypass; show an action forbidden by the declared plan policy.
repair: Reconcile provider events and server entitlements, then verify allowed grace, downgrade and replay behavior.
branch_decisions: Use the effective plan transition and documented grace period, not only a payment-provider event timestamp. Events may be delayed or out of order. Identify the protected server capability and whether a later authoritative event correctly reconciles it; a retained badge or invoice alone is not product access.
operational_method: Record authoritative event identity/version, provider state and the entitlement reducer rule. Feed owned events in order, then deliver an older active event after a newer cancellation and observe which generation controls the protected capability. Do not order unrelated events solely by arrival timestamp. Grace periods and corrective reconciliation are product policy; a stale badge is not continued server entitlement.
